question_text:
Consider the distribution curve of $X \sim \mathrm{N}(3, 4^2)$ shown:

Copy the above graph, and on the same set of axes sketch the distribution curve for:

subparts.final_answer: $\text{A horizontal translation of } \text{N}(3, 4^2) \text{ to the left by 2 units, centered at } x = 1$

mark_breakdown.desc: Indicating the curve has the same shape and spread as $\text{N}(3, 4^2)$
Correctly sketching the curve centered at $\mu = 1$

subparts.solution: The distribution $\text{N}(1, 4^2)$ has the same standard deviation $\sigma = 4$ as $\text{N}(3, 4^2)$, so the bell curve has the identical shape and height, but is shifted horizontally to be centered at mean $\mu = 1$ rather than $\mu = 3$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Changing the mean shifts the curve horizontally without altering its shape.
step_by_step: Draw the bell curve with peak centered at $x = 1$.
Ensure the height of the peak and width match $\text{N}(3, 4^2)$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Changing the height or width of the curve despite standard deviation remaining the same.

subparts.final_answer: $\text{A narrower and taller bell curve centered at } x = 3$

mark_breakdown.desc: Indicating the curve is centered at the same mean $\mu = 3$
Correctly sketching a taller, narrower curve corresponding to $\sigma = 2$

subparts.solution: The distribution $\text{N}(3, 2^2)$ has the same mean $\mu = 3$ as $\text{N}(3, 4^2)$, but a smaller standard deviation $\sigma = 2 < 4$. Therefore, the curve is centered at $x = 3$, but is narrower and has a significantly higher peak.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Decreasing the standard deviation concentrates the area closer to the mean, increasing the peak height.
step_by_step: Draw a curve with a higher peak and narrower spread than $\text{N}(3, 4^2)$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Drawing the curve wider when standard deviation decreases.

subparts.final_answer: $\text{A wider and flatter bell curve centered at } x = 2$

mark_breakdown.desc: Correctly sketching a flatter, wider curve corresponding to standard deviation $\sigma = 8$

subparts.solution: The distribution $\text{N}(2, 64)$ has mean $\mu = 2$ and standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{64} = 8$. Compared to $\text{N}(3, 4^2)$, the curve is centered slightly to the left at $x = 2$, but is much wider and flatter because $\sigma = 8 > 4$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A variance of $64$ gives $\sigma = 8$, which doubles the spread compared to $\sigma = 4$, lowering the peak height.
step_by_step: Draw a wider, flatter curve with approximately half the peak height of $\text{N}(3, 4^2)$.
